mechanism.name: Ye / 异方差弱无效 IV

sampling.dependence: iid individuals conditional on frozen coefficient vectors. One hundred independent Binomial(2,.5) SNPs and mutually independent U/epsilon_A/epsilon_Y; heteroskedastic exposure noise retained. No baseline covariates or LD data.

assumptions: Z与潜在U独立；GENIUS加性结构限制；异方差相关矩非退化；不要求所有SNP满足排除限制

properties.notes: No baseline observed covariates: dimension/effective_dimension=0. There are 100 active candidate instruments (not 100 observed confounders). Explicit product delta_j*Z_j*epsilon_A creates heteroskedasticity; outcome mean is linear. No claim of high-dimensional confounding. Baseline-dimension convention: p=0, effective_p=0, baseline_columns=[]; instruments, posttreatment variables, time points and network nodes are excluded. Reference sample size n_ref=128 independent subjects (the CPU interface-check setting), p/n_ref=0.00000000; high_dimensional=false refers to baseline p in this stated setting, not the full observed-column count. n remains a runtime argument; reassess the dimension/sample-size regime if n or p changes rather than treating this tag as a guarantee for arbitrary scaling.

truth.derivation: Analytic unit exposure effect beta=.4; independently recovered via heteroskedastic covariance ratios and actual-generator conditional first/second moments.

adaptations: Original Section6.1 structural equations, noise variances and four SNP-type proportions retained. New, fully recorded one-time coefficient realization uses Python random.Random(104729); author frozen coefficient vectors/seed were not supplied in the read text. This does not reproduce published Monte Carlo tables.
SNP type groups use fixed index blocks; SNPs are iid and this is a deterministic labelling of the source proportions. Coefficients fixed across repeated samples, never treated as a new family.
All four settings are declared; small CPU samples n=128 are interface checks, not the original n=10000/100000 estimator experiment. No LD/UK-Biobank or covariate supplement scenarios are claimed.
